question.problem:
The point $P$ with coordinates $(5,3)$ lies on the curve $y=f(x).$ Find the point $Q$ that must lie on $y=f(\frac{1}{4}x).$

The coordinates of $Q$ are $(${{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}$).$
question.worked_solution:
The function $y=f(\frac{1}{4}x)$ represents a stretch of the function $y=f(x)$ by a factor of $4$ parallel to the $x$-axis. This has the effect of multiplying the $x$-coordinates of all points on $y=f(x)$ by $4.$

Therefore, the point $(5,3)$ on $f(x)$ is mapped to the point $(4\cdot 5,3)=(20,3),$ and this point must lie on the graph of $y=f(\frac{1}{4}x)$
